correctness.rationale: Reconstructed duality for Heyting maps h=f^{-1}: a bounded f must send each maximal b_i to b_(u_i); the equation f(↑a_i)=↑f(a_i) forces adjacent-or-equal target upper indices and uniquely determines f(a_i). Thus zero-winding ±1/0 increment words (sum zero) and two extremal windings (sum ±m) give the total count. A zero-winding walk on only m steps cannot traverse all m edges; its traversed arc has k≤⌊m/2⌋ edges, hence f(P_m) is an alternating path with k minima and k+1 maxima. Restriction of upsets to this induced image poset is surjective; upper-set counts are F_(2k+3), whereas an automorphism image has L_(2m). Inclusion-exclusion of closed reflexive-path walks hitting both endpoints gives m(B_m,k−2B_m,k−1+B_m,k−2). Independently enumerated m=3..6 bounded maps and exact histograms: m3 {2:3,5:18,18:6}, m4 {2:4,5:56,13:16,47:8}, m5 {2:5,5:150,13:100,123:10}, m6 {2:6,5:372,13:432,34:36,322:12}. Those finite values corroborate the all-m argument.
residual_risks: Counts images of dual Heyting algebra homomorphisms, not merely image sizes of arbitrary monotone maps.

value.rationale: Exact cardinalities of endomorphic images are intrinsic and usable invariants of a natural infinite family of regular finite Heyting algebras. The full Fibonacci–Lucas spectrum and multiplicities identify strong sparsity and symmetry beyond any undifferentiated monotone-map count or textbook sequence identity.
residual_risks: m≥3 only, no inter-crown homomorphisms or full endomorphism monoid multiplication.
Finite enumeration is supporting evidence, not the proof for arbitrary m.

final_claim: For m≥3 the finite Heyting endomorphisms of the cyclic crown H_m=Up(P_m) correspond to based closed lazy walks on C_m; their count is m[2+Σ_j m!/(j!j!(m-2j)!)] and the complete image-cardinality spectrum consists of F_(2k+3), 0≤k≤⌊m/2⌋, and L_(2m), with multiplicities given by the trace inclusion-exclusion formula.
limitations: m≥3 only, no inter-crown homomorphisms or full endomorphism monoid multiplication.
Finite enumeration is supporting evidence, not the proof for arbitrary m.
